questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was decisive for my choice of destination that it had to be outside Europe as I wanted to experience a completely different culture and challenge myself. In addition, I chose California because of the good range of sociology courses and, of course, because of the good weather and vibes.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had a fantastic exchange stay with a lot of cool experiences both in terms of study, social and unique experiences. There are really good opportunities to try some exciting courses within many different areas of interest. I found that it was a different way of studying with less homework and more small take home exams that you don't have to be nervous about. It gave room to enjoy the time outside the lectures.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
There were some good information meetings about what to do before departure. However, there were many time-consuming processes, so I would recommend that you start applying for a visa etc. as early as possible. In addition, it is a good idea to talk to others who are going on an exchange or have been, if you are in doubt about something. 
Upon arrival, I recommend being accompanied by other exchange students and finding the office associated with exchange students on campus so you know where to go if you have questions.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was accompanied by five other Danes who were going on exchange at the same university. We had all been given a room in the international house on campus where there were resident assistants who you could ask for advice. Otherwise, a lot of information and experiences were exchanged with the other international students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There were a lot of new things to get used to and a lot of information at once, but I didn't experience any problems with not getting enough information.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It was possible to make an online application to get a place in international housing on campus, which I did.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: It was mandatory to choose one of three different meal plans, which you paid in advance, after which you got a food card that you could use in the mini-markets and canteens on campus. It worked okay, but the selection wasn't always that good. In addition, shopping on campus was a bit expensive compared to the prices in supermarkets outside the campus. I would recommend taking the smallest meal plan as otherwise it may be difficult to spend all the money on the card and these cannot be refundet.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is a really good opportunity to get to know people from all over the world and to be close to many other people in the same situation as yourself. It creates a strong unity. We lived four girls together in an apartment, so it is important to align expectations so that everyone feels comfortable.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
It was very expensive to live in international house - around DKK 10,000 per month. However, I still think it's worth it to have a safe place to live that is located at the university.
Those who lived in international house were typically a little younger (around 18-19 years old), which meant that you were sometimes in slightly different places in life. However, there were so many people that you could easily find someone you had something in common
with.There
were quite strict rules about parties and alcohol in international house.
It was illegal for people under 21 to drink alcohol and the police often shut down parties in the international house. Unfortunately, this meant that in the end there weren't that many social events as people were nervous about getting warnings.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was generally easy to apply. However, I think it was difficult to find out how ECTS should be converted and which courses corresponded to my level of study. It took some time to get used to.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
I found the most important information at
reciprocity.uceap.universityofcalifornia.edu
. It is well described there what must be done upon arrival. I recommend attending KU's information meetings as this is where the most important information and deadlines are presented.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Both contact with the exchange supervisor and emails to the University of California were useful for clarifying questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Unfortunately, not all the courses I had hoped to attend were offered in the two quarters I was on exchange. Therefore, I had to find some alternatives, but it was not difficult to find other exciting courses. However, I had to be a little creative with which courses to choose.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The most important thing is to start early so that you have time to clarify questions that arise along the way. It is a good idea to apply for courses as soon as you have the opportunity to get a place before they are all taken. In addition, it is a good idea to reserve an appointment at the embassy early to get a student visa in time.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was really happy with most of my courses, but I was also unlucky with a few of them. It was mainly because I did not have access to all the courses I had hoped for from home and therefore I had to take courses that did not interest me as much.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level was not as high as in Denmark, so it wasn't difficult to keep up. However, I still thought there were interesting courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There were both midterms and exams, which meant that you had tests approximately every two months. However, these tests were not that difficult as the subjects in question had just been dealt with in the lessons. I mainly had lectures in large lecture rooms and not so much group teaching in smaller groups.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: I was away for 1 semester corresponding to 2 quarters in California. In the first quarter I had the courses: Crime and Society, Predicting the Future and Genetics and Society. In the second quarter I had the courses: Climate and Civilization and Humans are Cultural Animals

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I loved the course Crime and Society because it is within my primary area of interest, the professor was phenomenal and the themes and guest lectures were really exciting. Predicting the Future was also a really exciting and different course about how we try to predict the future in different ways, from computer algorithms to Tarot cards. Genetics and Society was also a very interesting course on the social effects of the “genetic revolution”: eugenics, genetic discrimination, and stratification.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I bought a car with three other students. It was an old car so there were some unforeseen costs associated with it. Also traveling around California is expensive but so worth it!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing was way more expensive than I had thought. Fitness on campus, transportation by bus and train was free for students. Food was more expensive than I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were so many clubs and sports teams to join on campus. Very good selection.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were many good events to take part in. In addition, there were multiple sports matches which were nice to go to.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There were many events in international house which were fun to participate in. It is especially nice to participate in many activities at the beginning to get to know people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend going around the city and seeing the different areas, going to the beach and to other big cities and national parks in California.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: There were some things that were very different from Denmark, but you get used to that quickly. There was nothing that was really challenging. I experienced that it can be difficult to get a close relationship with the Americans.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: They are generally very open and welcoming, so it is easy to get to talk to new people. However, I did not get to create long-term relationships with Americans as I was mostly with exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There were not really any cultural differences that I found challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The culture and food was very inspired by the Mexican since it was close to the border. In addition, there was a lot of diversity, which was exciting and, of course, good weather and happy people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Spend as much time as possible socializing, experiencing all the amazing places in California and try surfing.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Check if the Duolingo language tests are still accepted at UC San Diego. It is much cheaper and easier than the alternatives. Seek a waiver for the expensive health insurance offered by the university. I can recommend ISO International Student Health Insurance which costs half as much.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the experiences I had along the way. It is so rewarding and at the same time you get to challenge yourself in a really cool way.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: That you had to deal with things yourself. You are so far away from home and you have to cope with the challenges you encounter and that makes you really strong and independent.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Just do it. You will not regret it!!!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
